extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors, copyeditors, and publishers preparing and editing scholarly and general publications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, editing, and publishing manuscripts, including punctuation, quotations, source citations, reference lists, publisher agreements, copyright, and format conventions across print and electronic formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotations — basic principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy; attribution and fair use; commonly known facts and expressions; credit and permission for quotations; danger of skewed meaning; paraphrase vs. quotation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain original meaning (13.51); prefer accurate transcription and correct attribution (13.6); consider fair-use and permission requirements (4.64, 4.75, 4.84, 4.92); use paraphrase when appropriate (4.89, 11.17, 13.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotation formatting (block vs. run-in; length; indentation; paragraphs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on beginning quotations in text, indentation for block quotations, run-in quotations vs. block, and treatment of paragraphs within quotations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Block-quotation indentation and guidelines (2.11, 2.19; 13.9-10); run-in quotations vs block (13.9-10); paragraphing inside quotations (2.19, 13.22, 13.32-33, 13.35); converting block quotations to run-in (13.31); length considerations for quotations and poetry extracts (13.10, 13.25-29).

rubrics_metrics.name: Brackets and editorial interpolations in quotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of brackets for adjustments in capitalization, tenses, pronouns; editorial interpolations and clarifications; marking missing or illegible words; use of [sic] and glosses or translations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust capitalization and tense with brackets (13.12, 13.18, 13.21, 13.53); indicate editorial interpolations and clarifications (6.99, 6.103); use brackets for missing/illegible words (13.59); include glosses or translations in brackets when needed (6.96, 6.99); mark errors in original with sic (6.73, 13.61).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotation marks — choice and punctuation interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for double vs. single quotation marks, British vs. US practice, closing marks, directional/smart marks, inverted and split-level quoting, and interaction with other punctuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatives to quotation marks discussed (6.91, 11.11, 11.19, 13.42); British-style and other variations (6.9, 13.30); closing quotation marks rules (6.9-11); directional/smart characters and file cleanup (2.85, 6.115); single vs double use and when single is preferred (7.58, 13.30-31); punctuation combinations with quotation marks (6.9-11, 6.114).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotations — punctuation, capitalization, and integration with surrounding text
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalization within quotations, punctuation that accompanies quotations, assimilation into surrounding text, introductory phrases, and placement relative to surrounding sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize initial letter appropriately (13.18-21); introductory words and phrases before quotations (13.14-16); assimilation of quotations into text (3.15, 13.11-12); punctuation rules for run-in and block quotations and text following quotations (2.12, 2.21, 13.24, 13.68-72).

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation — general principles and manuscript handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic function of punctuation, typographic considerations, marking manuscripts and proofs for punctuation, electronic file cleanup, and multiple marks at the same place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic function (6.1); typographic considerations for electronic publications (6.2-6, 6.14); marking manuscript and proofs (2.93, 2.95, 2.124, 2.132); electronic file cleanup and semantic/markup concerns (2.80, 2.82n1); treatment of multiple marks and summarized guidance (6.122-26, table 6.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question marks — uses and special cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage of question marks in different sentence types, relation to other punctuation, inverted question marks in Spanish, marking proofs, and when to omit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Question marks uses and spacing (6.68-70); punctuation interactions (with commas, ellipses, parentheses); inverted marks in Spanish works (11.19, 11.62); marking proofs for question marks (2.132); guidance on omission in certain contexts (6.69).

rubrics_metrics.name: Semicolons — uses and interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: When to use semicolons between clauses and in complex lists, and how semicolons interact with other punctuation and source citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General uses in independent clauses and series (6.56-60); semicolons in series of elements where internal commas exist (6.60, 6.129); other punctuation interactions (closing quotation marks, parentheses, ellipses); use in source citations for certain classical works and complex entries (14.57; 15.7, 15.22, 15.24, 15.28, 15.30).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commas and the serial (Oxford) comma
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on comma use, comma with conjunctions and lists, and explicit statement on serial (Oxford) commas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules on commas in series and with conjunctions (6.19-21, 6.23); recommendation and discussion of serial comma use (6.19-21, 6.23, 8.165, 14.135); interaction with ampersands and punctuation in series (6.21).

rubrics_metrics.name: Run-in quotations — assimilation and punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles for run-in quotations: assimilation into surrounding text, capitalization rules, multiple paragraphs, poetry and drama exceptions, and punctuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defined and contrasted with block quotations (13.9, 13.11-12); capitalization rules for run-in quotations (13.19, 13.21); handling multiple paragraphs (13.32-33, 13.35); punctuation specifics (colons, commas, quotation marks, slashes) and text citation rules for run-in quotations (13.14-16, 13.29-31, 13.68-69).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference lists — format, order, and manuscript preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure and formatting of reference lists, order of entries (alphabetical vs chronological), cross-checking, manuscript submission guidelines, hanging indentation, and metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format examples and variations (15.9, 15.22, fig. 15.1); ordering: alphabetical preferred, chronological when appropriate (2.63, 15.11, 15.18-19); hanging indentation (1.63, 2.24); cross-checking references (2.32, 2.63, 15.21); manuscript prep instructions and type size (2.24, 14.67, 15.17).

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened citations and criteria for short forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and format for shortened citations in notes and text, relation to full citations, and discouraged forms such as idem/op. cit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic structure and examples for short forms (14.29-36); use with authors' names, journals, chapters, multiauthor volumes, legal and classical works; cross-reference to full citation (14.31); discourage idem, op. cit., loc. cit. (14.35-36); guidance on use vs ibid. (1.124, 13.66, 14.34, 14.48).

rubrics_metrics.name: Source citations for quotations and texts
rubrics_metrics.description: How to cite quotations and textual extracts: full vs shortened citations; placement (text citations, footnotes); block-quotation citations; citations within quoted material; special cases for poetry and non-English materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text-citation guidance for quotations, block quotations, and notes (13.64-72; 15.26, 15.28, 15.40); handling quotations from secondary sources (14.260, 14.291, 15.56); rules for poetry, drama, and run-in quotations (13.25-29, 13.47); non-English citation considerations (11.x references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference works — formatting and online considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific guidance for reference works: HTML formatting, hyperlinks, indexing, online versions, and source-citation norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HTML and hyperlink guidance for reference works (1.118; 1.120); indexes and indexing principles for reference works (16.26, 16.32); online-version notes and metadata (1.118, 14.233); source-citation guidance for reference works and online access (14.103, 14.232-34).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific and technical works — structural and citation norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for scientific and technical publishing: abstracts, sections and subsections, numbering, use of SI units, tables, titles, preprints, and author-date reference preferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract and section guidance (1.93, 1.95, 1.57); author-date reference system preference and database citations (14.3, 14.257; 15.5); units of measurement and SI guidance (10.49, 10.51-59); tables and figures standards (3.48, 3.86); preprints and continuous publishing model notes (1.113, 1.82, 1.104).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishers and publishing agreements — rights and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Publisher-related standards: addresses and metadata, publishing agreements' basic provisions, authors' warranties and limits, rights to reproduction and distribution, 'no derivatives' clauses, subsidiary rights, open-access models, and publisher responsibilities for copyright tasks and permissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing agreements basic provisions and examples (4.52-63; figs. 4.1-2); author warranties and limitations (4.52, 4.70, 4.72, 4.73); rights to reproduction/distribution and subsidiary rights (4.51; 4.17-18); no-derivatives clauses and multilingual rights (4.62, 4.64); publisher duties on copyright and permissions (4.32, 4.70-71, 4.76n1); open-access considerations (4.52, 4.61, 4.66).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright, public-domain, and reproduction issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards around reproduction and copyright: when works enter the public domain, derivative works, government-produced works, permissions, scans and scanning, and copyright dates for reprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproduction and copyright rules (4.13, 4.34, 4.51, 4.64); public-domain timing and derivative-work treatment (4.19, 4.20, 4.22, 4.27); government-produced works guidance (4.21, 4.44, 4.68, 4.75); permissions sourcing and fees including out-of-business rights (4.82, 4.104); scanning and OCR considerations for illustrations and older works (2.27, 2.47, 14.162).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript preparation — running heads, title metadata, and front/back matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on creating manuscript elements: running heads (content selection and omission), title metadata, recto/verso page handling, front matter components (copyright/page ordering), and submission instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Running heads: choice of content, omission rules, proofing, and shortening (1.10-16; 2.76; 1.11, 2.76, 14.47); title metadata and running-head linkage (1.12); recto pages and pagination conventions (1.5, 1.4, 1.49); front/back matter placement and manuscript page specifications (1.4, 1.19, 1.63).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading, marking proofs, and permissible changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for proofreading manuscripts and proofs, how to mark punctuation and typographic elements, permissible changes to quoted and referenced materials, and handling revised proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marking manuscripts and proofs for punctuation and changes (2.93, 2.95, 2.124, 2.131-32); permissible changes to quotations and other materials (13.7, 13.8); proofreading items such as running heads, recto pages, and running feet (2.76, 2.114-15); handling revised proofs and version control (2.103-105, 1.112, 2.140).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexes and indexing principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on index organization: run-in style vs. runover, headings, alphabetizing, indexing names/titles, and indexes for specific types of materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index organizing principles and differences from search engines (1.110-111, 16.2, 16.7); run-in style and runover lines for indexes (run-in style references; 16.26, 16.28, 16.137); alphabetizing rules and index headings (16.74, 16.93, 16.96); special indexing treatment for authors, firstlines, titles, and reference works (16.145; 16.26).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-English materials — treatment of punctuation, quotation, and titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Special rules for handling non-English quoted materials, punctuation (e.g., inverted question marks), quotation marks (guillemets), capitalization and transliteration, and citation practices for translated or transliterated texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-English punctuation and quotation guidance (11.xx references: inverted question marks in Spanish, guillemets in French/Italian, split-level quoting in German, etc.); capitalization and title-style differences (11.6, 11.27, 14.98-99); transliteration and romanization notes (transliteration references; 11.75, 11.110).

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital and electronic publishing concerns (URLs, DOIs, reflowable formats)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for including URLs/DOIs in text and source citations, short forms for DOIs/URLs, handling of reflowable formats for illustrations and line breaks, and electronic-file cleanup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: URLs and DOIs handling in text and citations (14.10, 14.17-18, 6.8); short forms for DOIs/URLs (14.10); reflowable-format considerations (illustration placement, line breaks, navigation; 1.123; 3.8); electronic file cleanup and smart characters (2.80, 2.85, 6.115).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables, figures, and illustrations — placement and typographic rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for tables and illustrations: placement in print and reflowable formats, typographic treatment (rules and shading), table punctuation, and figure captions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustration placement guidance for print and e-books (3.8; 1.107; 3.11, 3.25-27); table rules, indentation, and punctuation in tables (3.53, 3.57, 3.58, 3.74, 3.86; table 3.12); typographic considerations such as shading and resolution (3.19, 3.43; resolution p. 986).

rubrics_metrics.name: Names, publishers' names, and bibliographic metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: How to render authors' names, publishers' names (imprints, parent companies), when to omit, abbreviations, and preferred forms in source citations and metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred forms for publishers' names and when to omit (14.133-41; 14.127, 14.128); handling imprints and parent companies (14.138-41); authors' names in citations and shorthand (14.30-33; initials, et al., ordering; 15.12, 15.33, 14.76).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions, royalties, and subsidiary rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy around permissions requests, fees, handling royalties (including failure to pay), subsidiary rights and rights to reprints and reissued editions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissions procedures and publisher responsibilities (4.70, 4.71, 4.76n1); royalties and failures to pay (4.37); subsidiary rights and their relation to royalties and reproduction rights (4.17-18, 4.64, 4.69); reprint rights and copyright dates for reprints (4.55, 4.64, 1.23).
